title: ID0461159-DC/Si-D/IE-[MP / S2 170003301] SECC Offline Causing Cable Lock
description:
Reported behavior/issue- SECC Offline Causing Cable Lock
Solution: EcoG lost communication -> v8.0.5 update
1. TECHNICAL OVERVIEW
The charge began at 09:20 Irish time and terminated within seconds (0 kWh
delivered). Immediately afterwards, the unit reported Faulted – SECC is offline
at 09:24 and again at 09:31, remaining in fault until an on-site emergency cable
release was performed at 11:04 Irish time.
From the data and CCTV, it appears the SECC module lost communication during the
Finishing phase, preventing the unlock command from reaching the latch actuator.
The unit later self-recovered without a full reboot.
Please confirm:
* Whether this failure mode is known on SiCharge D hardware, and if firmware
updates exist that ensure automatic latch release when SECC communication
drops during Finishing.
* Any recommended diagnostic steps or parameter settings (e.g., watchdog
timers, SECC restart intervals, or unlock-on-fault options) to mitigate
recurrence.
* Whether Siemens recommends a preventive SECC reboot schedule or other
operational measure for high-use sites.
2. LOG DATA
If possible, please extract and share controller and SECC logs for 09:15 – 09:40
UTC on 10 Nov 2025 from this unit so we can verify the internal event chain.
3. FIRMWARE CONFIRMATION
Kindly confirm the current firmware versions (main controller, SECC, and power
module) for this unit, and whether the auto-unlock logic is standard in the
latest certified release.
This is the only known occurrence at Galway, but it resulted in a prolonged
customer lock-in and manual intervention, so we’d like to apply any corrective
update or configuration Siemens recommends.

From the data and CCTV, it appears the SECC module lost communication during the Finishing phase, preventing the unlock command from reaching the latch actuator. The unit later self-recovered without a full reboot.
Please confirm:
Whether this failure mode is known on SiCharge D hardware, and if firmware updates exist that ensure automatic latch release when SECC communication drops during Finishing.
Any recommended diagnostic steps or parameter settings (e.g., watchdog timers, SECC restart intervals, or unlock-on-fault options) to mitigate recurrence.
Whether Siemens recommends a preventive SECC reboot schedule or other operational measure for high-use sites.
2. Log data
If possible, please extract and share controller and SECC logs for 09:15 – 09:40 UTC on 10 Nov 2025 from this unit so we can verify the internal event chain.
3. Firmware confirmation
Kindly confirm the current firmware versions (main controller, SECC, and power module) for this unit, and whether the auto-unlock logic is standard in the latest certified release.
This is the only known occurrence at Galway, but it resulted in a prolonged customer lock-in and manual intervention, so we’d like to apply any corrective update or configuration Siemens recommends.
Many thanks,
Colin Barry
Brite EV Charging Ltd

additional_info.subject: Re: ID0461159-DC/Si-D/TR-[MP / S2 170003301] SECC Offline Causing Cable Lock CRM:03056000473
additional_info.body:
Hi Francisco,
Thanks for confirming and for the quick analysis, much appreciated.
Yes, this is the first instance we have seen of this issue at Galway Retail Park. The logs, CCTV and UCC record all align with your assessment – SECC communication interruption during Finishing, session continuing for approximately 18 minutes, and the EV remaining locked until manual emergency release.
It is worth noting that this 18-minute continuation does not appear in the GreenFlux or CPO session data, which shows the transaction ending after only a few seconds (0 kWh). We now understand this is because the SECC loss prevented the OCPP StopTransaction and power data from being transmitted, so the backend recorded the charge as completed while the power module locally continued to supply current. This distinction is important for audit accuracy and any future root-cause reviews.
Could you please confirm the internal metering delta (kWh delivered) for EVSE IE-GFX-E170003301-2 between 09:20 and 09:38 Irish time on 10 November. We estimate roughly 2–8 kWh may have been delivered, given the unit was already in the Finishing or taper phase, but we would like the exact value from the charger’s local power trace.
We are happy to proceed with the latest firmware update you mentioned. Please confirm the rollout procedure and timeline for this specific unit (IE-GFX-E170003301-2) and whether it can be performed remotely or will require a field visit.
Given that the incident resulted directly from a hardware or software communication fault, we also request that Siemens cover the associated UCC intervention cost (€1.75 per minute × ~18 minutes ≈ €31.50). The intervention was required only because the unit failed to release the cable automatically after the SECC fault.
Please confirm:
- That this issue will be logged internally under warranty or service records for traceability.
- Whether the upcoming firmware version fully includes auto-unlock protection in the event of SECC communication loss.
Additional update (11 November 2025):
We have had a similar SECC-related fault this morning

additional_info.body:
Hello Colin,
Thanks for the quick feedback.
The meter data is
55942 Wh = 55.942 kWh
What I see is that the EV was on 29% when it reach the site and it ended with 98%.
The update is ready to be performed. We can do the update between 8am and 5pm, please let me know what time fits you best. Jason told me that he can arrange someone to go there to proceed with the update to make sure everything runs smoothly, so please find me a time and we will do it together.
The intervention cost must be aligned with Jason as well, from Tech Support, I am only capable of providing the troubleshooting, analysis and solution.
Regarding your question of unlocking the cable, it is only indirectly related to the charger. According to the international norm:
The EV is the one responsible for locking the plug, in this case, we couldn't remove it since we couldn't stop the session from the charger, but when you stop from the EV, it must unlock.
I checked the timestamp you provided to me today and found that the reason why it went wrong it was because the system needed to do a FW calibration of the voltage reading and the session failed, when the calibration was succesfully performed, it restarted the EcoG and that is the reason why you saw that error.
~4mins later we could do the charging again:
I will wait patiently for your feedback.
Thank you for your time and patience.
Best regards,
Francisco

Re: ID0461159-DC/Si-D/IE-[MP / S2 170003301] SECC Offline Causing Cable Lock CRM:03056000473
additional_info.body:
Hi Francisco,
Thanks for the clear analysis. Here is what this means for us in simple terms and what we propose next.
Root cause and behaviour
The unit performed a firmware self-calibration of the voltage reading. During that moment the SECC communication dropped, so the backend saw the session end while the charger kept power active locally for about 18 minutes. Because DC voltage remained above 60 V, the plug stayed mechanically locked in line with IEC 61851-23. The lock released only after the emergency procedure.
